title: Find the leaking cable core with a hand-crank insulation tester
instruction: One core of this cable has failed insulation. Test all three cores with the hand-crank insulation tester and its red probe before moving any flag (the tester only reads while its handle is being cranked), then push the flag beside the failed core over to red, put the probe back in its holder and let go of everything.
context: Electricians (O*NET 47-2111.00, also 49-2092.00) test a cable's cores with a hand-crank insulation tester, which makes its test voltage only while the generator handle turns and drops the reading when cranking stops. One hand cranks while the other holds the line probe on the conductor, so the reading needs both hands at once and the prod moves from core to core while the crank keeps turning. The result is a diagnosis (read the needle, then mark the failed core), not just a hold or a turn.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); heights above the table top. Insulation tester: fixed steel case 12 x 12 x 12 cm, 3 kg, centred x 30, y -22, with a dial on its near face (needle at 'off' when the handle is still, red band below 1 megohm). On top a vertical-axis hand crank: 4.5 cm bar ending in a free-spinning black knob 2.5 cm across and 3 cm tall (centre 15 cm high); the circle of the knob runs x 25.5 to 34.5. Crank friction 0.03 N m (0.7 N at the knob), no flywheel; the knob starts at y -17.5. Terminal block: wooden plate 14 x 22 x 3 cm, 3 kg, at x 30, y 14, with three brass test studs 2.5 cm across, tops 6 cm high, at y +6, +14 and +22 (plain posts, nothing to clip to). Behind each stud at x 35 a toggle flag: 5 cm lever with a 2.5 cm green tab on a pin 3 cm high, upright (green) or tipped 40 degrees away from the robot (red), 0.04 N m detent. Red test prod: 2.5 cm grip, 12 cm long, with a 3 cm tip of 1.2 cm across, 0.06 kg, standing tip-down in a holder cup (flared mouth) at x 24, y +28, grip centre 10 cm high. Cable: 1 m of three-core 1.5 mm2 PVC flex, isolated from any supply, clamped behind the block; each core is soldered to the underside of one stud and its far end is insulated and left open. A copper earth bar under the block is wired to the tester's earth terminal. The fault: a 0.5 megohm resistor hidden under the block joins one core's stud to the earth bar; the other two cores read over 200 megohm (shown as infinity). Which core is faulty is set per trial (any of the three; the middle one by default) and nothing on the table shows it. Tester: 500 V hand-crank insulation tester, output current limited below 2 mA.
scoring: Measured with a ruler and a stopwatch. A core counts as tested when the prod's tip rests on its stud (within 2 mm of the top and 6.5 mm of the axis, prod within 30 degrees of vertical) for 1 s while the crank turns at 0.4 rev/s or more (speed over the last 0.5 s). 0 at once and for good if a flag is pushed to red before all three cores were tested, a flag is pushed on a healthy core (any core other than the one configured as faulty for the trial), the prod is dropped (falls over or lies low away from its holder), or a gripper touches a stud; also 0 if no core was tested. Otherwise 0.25 for one or two cores tested; 0.5 for all three tested but the faulty core's flag not at red; 0.75 for all three tested and only the faulty core's flag at red, but the prod not back in its holder (within 1 cm and 10 degrees), a gripper within 3 cm of the prod, knob or flags, or not still; 1.0 with all of that met and the prod, flags and crank still (1 mm, 1 degree) for 1 s.
reset_notes: Stand the prod in its holder, turn the crank so the knob is at y -17.5, tip all three flags back to green, set the needle to off. Out of the robot's sight, move the 0.5 megohm resistor to the stud chosen for the next trial (in simulation, set MEGGER_FAULTY to 0, 1 or 2) and check all three readings by hand with the tester. Touch the earth lead to each stud to discharge it.
fidelity: Rigid bodies; the crank is a revolute joint with 0.03 N m Coulomb friction, the flags are hinges with a drive detent. The test voltage, 1 s timer, needle and readings are computed in code from the configured faulty core (MEGGER_FAULTY, default the middle one). The cable, the prod's lead and the earth lead are not simulated. No electricity.
